correctness.rationale: For a nonempty witness set in one part, the complement of its diamond is exactly that part. Successive Boolean exclusion of earlier peeled parts makes such witnesses definable. On the core, every used color has representatives in at least two core parts, so every successor color can be matched while avoiding the current part. Matching peeled successors in the same peeled part proves bisimulation; the definable parts and color tests distinguish all proposed classes. Hence the atom and cardinality formulas hold. Injectivity within each part is also required for full generation: the all-subfamilies private-color test in the Finding is read as an equivalence for empty core, as its proof specifies. A sequential peeling order forbids its first i-1 distinct witness colors in part i. Exchanging any ascending pair of sizes minimizes the maximum n_i+i-1 in descending order; suffix palettes containing their designated witness attain the bound. This handles k=1 and zero generators. Depth is bounded by one new diamond per round, using complementation for a final singleton part. In the chain example each still-unsplit repeated color is visible from every part; only the part with a private current type is detected in the next refinement, splitting just the next chain color. This yields exactly k-1 strict steps, including the final two-part step.
residual_risks: The Finding's shorthand 'Equivalently' must not be read as waiving injectivity within parts; a two-vertex one-part monochromatic example would contradict that reading. The proof explicitly retains injectivity.
The finite verifier was inspected, not executed; the unbounded argument is mathematical.
